What degraded

  • The deck shipped at the round cap at 6.988, 0.712 under round 2's 7.7 rung, with the art median 6.5 and the craft floor stood down at the cap.
  • The hero Caravan is a chassis model the judges charged in every round (flat window cutouts, the wing a slab from a long lens, the strut crossing the windows). Queued for the weekly pass as aviation-models-built-in-chassis.
  • Frames 5 and 8 carry the lastLight horizon's warm band behind the type, which the deck's one declared world can't change per frame. Queued.
  • c33, a TxDOT-credited photo caption on Dallas Innovates showing Merlin's Caravan in the test flights, is cited on frame 3 and printed nowhere. The integrity judge asked for one sentence carrying it, and the cap allowed only hard-fail repairs.
  • The new web edition was checked by its 765 automated reader checks. The browser test's screenshots went to the September 18th edition again, so the new page was not inspected by eye. Queued.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Software on the radio. Merlin's account of the Project Nexus kickoff, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Did software work the radio?

Merlin says TxDOT invited it to the Project Nexus kickoff at Fort Worth Alliance Airport on September 10th. It says its Merlin Pilot demonstrated AI-powered air traffic control communications. TxDOT's and the FAA's releases skip Merlin.

TxDOT's first phase tests helicopters and fixed-wing planes. Its first flights carry no passengers and collect data and validate routes. Medical and cargo logistics come next. The FAA says it will write rules from that data.

Counted from September 10th, October 8th is 28 days into the three years TxDOT gives Project Nexus.

Only Merlin's release names its Caravan, and only in a photo caption. None of the three releases says whether a pilot was aboard or prints a measured result. Is silence in all three the whole public record on both?

#ProjectNexus #TxDOT #FortWorth

The machine changed itself

  • Five machine items queued in knowledge/carousel/MACHINE_QUEUE.md and the arsenal rebuilt

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

Carousel no. 46 ships at the round cap, 6.988 against a ladder of 8.0, 7.7 and then ship. The panel medians were 6.614, 6.942 and 6.988. The art median is 6.5, and the craft floor stood down at the cap. The story is tx-2026-0205, admitted today. TxDOT launched the first phase of Project Nexus at Fort Worth Alliance Airport on September 10th. Merlin says it demonstrated AI-powered air traffic control communications there from a Cessna Caravan. Neither TxDOT's release nor the FAA's names Merlin, and none of the three releases says whether a pilot was aboard or prints a measured result. Two hard fails were found and repaired. In round 1 the deck said none of the releases says how the demonstration went, but Merlin's own release calls it safe and effective. The record table now reads PRINTS A RESULT, and compute.py scans the three releases for both silent rows instead of typing them. In round 3 the web edition carried "rather than removing the pilot", which Merlin's quote does not say. The claim and the article now say what the quote says, and the judge confirmed the repair. After the cap the gate sync found 1,096 on the close tracing to nothing, so that dek now reads "28 of 1,096 days", declared from compute.py. What the judges still charge: the chassis Caravan reads as a primitive model on most frames, frame 3 has an empty lower apron, and frames 5 and 8 carry a warm haze behind the type. A TxDOT-credited photo caption on Dallas Innovates (c33) shows Merlin's Caravan in the test flights, and the deck cites it without printing it. Worth knowing before posting, since the cover says neither agency's release names Merlin, which is true of the releases. The record: 102 items re-verified with a checked note, counted from the final ledger, tx-2026-0024's PUCT calendar rewritten from the live feed, and three items admitted (tx-2026-0205, tx-2026-0206, tx-2026-0207). All instruments read clean. Permissions: the no-stall hook was armed at 06:16:02 UTC and judged the session unattended, with the host's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED at 0. It refused nothing. prompt_audit lists six Agent dispatches with a 10 to 20 second permission wait as having waited on a human. No human was present and nothing was answered, so those read as the host's spawn latency. The reading in this payload was taken before the merge.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
